groups.intro: Whether and how the state credentials this profession — the regulatory model, credential type, authority, exams, fees, and renewal.

"board" means the State Medical Board

fields.meaning: Structured decomposition of the issuing authority — name, type (standalone board / shared board / division / department / joint), and any umbrella agency it sits within. Populated alongside the legacy free-text issuing_authority for back-compat.
Residency / supervised practice / apprenticeship — name varies, structure doesn't.
License renewal fee in US dollars (integer). Many statutes leave the amount to the board's discretion — leave null in that case.

fields.meaning: Professional ASSOCIATION the state references (e.g. for accreditation or CE provider approval) — 'American Podiatric Medical Association (APMA)', 'American Dental Association (ADA)'. Distinct from the certifying body. Null if not referenced.

fields.meaning: Is the credential MANDATORY to practice (or claim the title) in this state? True if practicing without it is prohibited; False if optional (e.g., voluntary certification that only protects the title for those who hold it).

groups.intro: Fields discovered specifically for this profession (auto-derived from its statutes; they vary profession to profession).

fields.meaning: The distinct license status categories a physician may hold beyond a standard active license, such as inactive, retired, volunteer, temporary, or administrative.

example.quote: A licensee who does not practice in the state may hold an inactive license. A person who practices in the state, however infrequently, shall hold an active license.

fields.meaning: Special additional requirements imposed on graduates of medical schools outside the United States or Canada, such as additional postgraduate training years, ECFMG certification, or separate examination standards.

example.value: Foreign medical graduates must meet requirements of AS 08.64.200(a)(3)-(5) and 08.64.255, complete three years of postgraduate training (or alternative board-approved proof of competency), and pass board-specified examinations.

fields.meaning: Whether physicians providing pain management services must obtain a separate registration or license from the board in addition to their standard medical license.
Specific statutory conditions under which a physician may prescribe drugs, including controlled substances, to patients seen only via telehealth rather than in person.

example.value: Board may not impose disciplinary sanctions for prescribing non-controlled substances via telehealth if follow-up care is available and records are shared with primary care provider with patient consent; controlled substances may also be prescribed if those conditions plus opioid limits are met. Prescribing in response to internet questionnaire or email without prior physician-patient relationship is prohibited.

Whether the state has enacted the Interstate Medical Licensure Compact, enabling eligible physicians to obtain expedited licenses in multiple member states.

example.value: Physician assistants may prescribe drugs (including controlled substances via telehealth) subject to the same conditions as physicians under AS 08.64.364; duties related to pain management and opioid use and addiction may not be delegated.
